title: 1901 c. Riverside Hotel & livery stables. Note privy on the bridge
description: The building, initially known as the Riverside Inn and managed by M. F. Thornton, later became Clark’s Inn, complete with livery stables behind it. David Clark, son of Allison, was known for offering carriage rides from the CPR to Clark’s Hotel, always distinguished by his top hat and pipe. In 1920, the hotel and livery stable were put up for sale, including all the furniture. The property featured five sleeping rooms, an office, a ladies’ parlor, and a large dining room. In the background is the uncovered bridge, opened in 1901 as a toll bridge. Note the privy located on the bridge between the first and second spans, just to the left of the pole. (Photo courtesy of Ralph Day)
